report.tagline: A Finnish smart ring that tracks sleep, readiness and activity, sold as a $350 to $400 ring plus a small monthly membership, and filed to go public in 2026.
report.simpleSummary: Oura is a ring that looks like jewellery but has sensors inside. You wear it day and night, and the app tells you how well you slept, how ready your body is today, and how active you were. You buy the ring once for about $350 to $400, then pay about $6 a month for the full app. It became the best-selling smart ring, sold 3.6 million rings in a year, and filed for a US stock market listing in September 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: Oura makes a smart ring with sensors for heart rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen and movement. The app turns this into Sleep, Readiness and Activity scores, plus features for stress, women's health (cycle and pregnancy insights), heart health and metabolic health with partners like Dexcom. An AI Advisor answers questions about your data. Oura also sells to employers, the US military and health partners.
howItWorks: A buyer orders a free sizing kit, picks a size, then buys the ring in a chosen finish.
The ring is worn 24/7 and needs charging about every 5 to 8 days.
Data syncs to the Oura app, which shows scores each morning.
A membership unlocks full scores, trends and features; without it the app shows very little.
Partner integrations, such as Dexcom glucose sensors and Natural Cycles, add more health data.
Oura sells rings directly, on Amazon and in stores like Best Buy and Target.
overview.valueProposition: Health tracking you forget you are wearing: a small, stylish ring that gives accurate sleep and recovery insights, without a screen or a bulky watch.

businessModel.summary: Oura earns twice from each customer: once when they buy the ring and again every month from the membership. It also earns from enterprise and government deals.

revenueStreams.detail: Rings at $350 to $400; most of revenue today. 3.6 million sold in a year.
About $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year; about 5 million paying members.
Employers, US Department of Defense and health partners.

businessModel.pricing: Ring from about $349 to $499 depending on finish (TechCrunch cites $350 to $400). Membership about $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year in the US. Prices differ in other countries.
costDrivers: Warranty replacements for battery and cracking issues
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take one new customer. They pay about $350 for the ring. After manufacturing, shipping and retailer cut, Oura may keep roughly half. Then they pay about $72 a year in membership, which costs Oura little to serve. With about 85% of members staying a year, a typical customer brings in about $350 plus $72 a year for several years, so the LTV (lifetime value) is likely $500 or more. Most of the profit after year one comes from the membership.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth and celebrity sightings
Retail in Best Buy, Target, Amazon and Costco
Partnerships with sports leagues, employers and the military
growth.moat: Oura has the strongest brand in smart rings, years of sleep data from millions of users and many patents. In 2025 it won a US trade case that blocked rivals like Ultrahuman and RingConn from importing some rings. Big companies like Samsung also make rings, so patents and brand matter.

northStar.metric: Paid members who wear the ring at least 5 nights a week

pmLessons: Form factor matters. A ring solved the 'I hate sleeping with a watch' problem.
Hardware plus subscription can work if the subscription keeps adding value.
Patents can protect a hardware business in a crowded market.
Users compare total cost: ring price plus fees. Be clear about what the fee buys.

interviewQuestions.question: Samsung's ring has no subscription. Should Oura drop its fee?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue mix, retention, perception; propose a hybrid free and paid tier, test before deciding.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Oura and WHOOP business models.
interviewQuestions.hint: Oura sells hardware plus low fee; WHOOP includes hardware in a higher fee. Discuss CAC, LTV, upgrade cycles.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to grow Oura among women.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a life stage, map needs, use sensors, define success metric and privacy guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you decide whether to build a screen into a future Oura product?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at user needs, form factor, battery trade-offs, and brand promise.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star metric would you pick for Oura?
interviewQuestions.hint: Regular wear by paid members; break into sales, activation, wear and retention.
